Command: Send away the mother bird before taking the young
Summary: One half of the mother-bird law of Deuteronomy 22:6-7: send away the mother bird before taking the young. Even in taking from nature, mercy was to limit what could be taken.
Commandment: Send away the mother bird before taking the young
Application: Scripture's stated reason, in the form of a promise: that it may be well with thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days (Deuteronomy 22:7). Mercy to the creature is joined to blessing on the keeper.
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason, in the form of a promise: that it may be well with thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days (Deuteronomy 22:7).
Function: One half of the mother-bird law of Deuteronomy 22:6-7: send away the mother bird before taking the young. Not a courtroom rule but a human one: this duty holds in every age. Scripture states the reason as a promise: that it may be well with thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days. It set the duty where it could be kept. Mercy to the creature is joined to blessing on the keeper.
